1.7 percent improvement in fuel economy resulting from weight reduction is 0.7 percent of fuel economy improvement due to the engine displacement times total drive ratio, (CID) x (N/V), reduction assumed for GM. This (CID) x (N/V) reduction is still applicable to GM as is the 1 percent and 0.7 percent improvement in fuel economy. This is discussed further in the preamble to the final rule.

EPA Fuel Economy Test Procedure and Related Road Load Horsepower Changes
.
American Motors Corporation (AMC) AMC estimates that the change of test procedure (i.e., increased road load horsepower approximately 30 percent higher than that specified in the 1977 test procedure) coupled with the tighter emission standard, will cause a fuel economy loss exceeding 10 percent.
Ford Motor Company. A substantial portion of Ford's response to the NPRM deals with the fuel economy impact of MY 1979 test procedures and emission standard. Ford Ford claims that the test procedure changes requiring higher chassis dynamometer loads, adopted by EPA for MY 1979 light trucks, cause a large penalty in light truck fuel economy. An in-depth Ford engineering study assessed this impact by means of four different technical methods
